egress.empty: No exits defined: one double-NAT exit is assumed.
egress.name: Name

egress.label: Label

modes.internal: Not an internet exit (NAT towards a DMZ, VLAN, VPN or branch)

egress.publicHint: One IPv4 address or a network of at least /24 per line, e.g. 203.0.113.208/29

warnings.noPublic: No public address: this exit is searched for every public IP that no exit claims.
warnings.dynamic: Public IP may change: besides its listed addresses, this exit is also searched for public IPs that no exit claims.
warnings.interfaces: Enter each line's interfaces (dstintf); without them a lookup cannot tell by which line a session left, and at moments when a line cannot be confirmed the search falls back to unclaimed addresses only.
warnings.publicNat: The NAT address is a public address: if the FortiGate holds it itself, the line is direct; set its type to Direct.
warnings.converted: Converted at the upgrade: while the converted exits stay without interfaces and unchanged, lookups treat them as one line, as the old NAT settings did; the NAT addresses of an exit added later are outside that. Enter each line's public address and interfaces (INSTALL.md section 13).

egress.serverRefused: The server did not accept the exit definition ({{code}}).

codes.setting_interface_invalid: An interface name has 1-35 characters, without control characters or leading/trailing spaces.
codes.setting_egress_name: An exit name has lower-case letters, digits and hyphens (at most 32 characters), e.g. hat-1.
codes.setting_egress_field: An exit has an unknown or missing field; the fields are label, mode (required), public, public_dynamic, transips, interfaces, port_preservation.
codes.setting_egress_dynamic: "Public IP may change" can only be chosen for an ISP NAT exit.
codes.setting_egress_mode: The NAT type must be direct, isp_nat, not_logged or internal.
codes.setting_egress_label: A label has at most 64 characters and no control characters.
codes.setting_egress_address: Invalid address: an IPv4 address or an IPv4 network of at least /24 is expected (the network address, e.g. 203.0.113.208/29).
codes.setting_ipv6_not_supported: IPv6 addresses are not supported in this version.
codes.setting_egress_overlap: A public or NAT address cannot be in two exits; the same transip is allowed only when the two exits have separate interfaces.
codes.setting_egress_direct: A direct exit needs at least one public address; it has no transip (the FortiGate uses the public address itself) and port preservation stays 'unknown'.
codes.setting_egress_not_logged: An exit that does not pass the FortiGate has only public addresses and a label.
codes.setting_egress_internal: An exit that is not an internet exit has only NAT addresses (at least one), interfaces and a label.
codes.setting_egress_port_preservation: Port preservation must be unknown, preserved or not_preserved.
codes.setting_egress_catch_all: At most one exit may have no NAT address (the one that covers unclaimed addresses).
codes.setting_egress_public_private: A public address cannot be a private (RFC 1918), shared (RFC 6598) or reserved address; enter the FortiGate's address behind the ISP router as the NAT address of an ISP NAT exit.
codes.setting_egress_isp_nat_direct: A line whose NAT address is its public address is direct: set its type to Direct.
codes.egress_duplicate_name: Two exits cannot have the same name.
